threads.body: [Testing] This variant inherits `collectMetadata` from `withType<Test>()`, but without `metadataConfig` its `testNewServerAt=true` telemetry is recorded as the default mode and becomes indistinguishable from the ordinary test run. Label the non-default JVM setting explicitly.

replies.body: `metadataConfig` labels agent configuration that changes telemetry (it becomes the `when` key in the generated metadata). `testNewServerAt` only changes how the test server binds — the telemetry is expected to be identical to the default run, which is what this task verifies — so recording it as `default` is intentional. Labeling it would publish a non-existent config option in the instrumentation docs.

replies.body: Thanks, switched to `CallDepth` in 6cb97416b5. `bindAndHandleImpl` is now advised unconditionally, and the advice only wraps the handler when it is the outermost bind call, so on 1.x the nested `bindAndHandle` call leaves the already wrapped flow alone.

threads.body: [Testing] The new `BadRequest` pass-through path is not exercised by the reused tests: `PekkoHttpServerParsingErrorTest` sends HTTP/1.1 requests, and the HTTP/2 suite only exercises successfully parsed requests. Please add a 2.x installed-agent test that triggers an HTTP/2 parsing rejection, asserts Pekko's 400 response, then sends a valid request on the same connection and checks its telemetry. This verifies that returning a non-request parsing result unchanged neither closes the connection nor disrupts subsequent request tracing.

replies.body: Added `testHttp2ParsingError` in 2c1efc019d. It sends an http/2 request with more headers than the default `max-header-count`, asserts that pekko-http answers it with 400, then sends a valid request on the same client and asserts that its server and controller spans are traced as usual.

threads.body: [Testing] The HTTP/2 fixture completes responses through `system.dispatcher`, so it does not cover the new completion-context boundary when application code completes a response on a separate executor. Add an installed-agent test that completes response promises on that executor with each request's context current, while requests with distinct parents overlap on one connection. Assert that each request retains its own server and controller spans, without inheriting another request's context.

replies.body: Added `testResponsesCompletedOnSeparateExecutor` in 2c1efc019d. A new fixture endpoint completes its responses after a random delay on a separate scheduled executor, with the request context current. The test sends 20 overlapping requests on one http/2 connection and asserts that each one is its own trace: a server span with no parent plus its controller span. The requests deliberately carry no `traceparent`. An extracted remote parent would override a leaked context and hide the leak, while without one a leaked context shows up as a server span parented to another request.

threads.body: [Testing] This shutdown is never reached: `PekkoHttpServerInstrumentationTestHttp2.setupServer()` returns `null`, so `AbstractHttpServerUsingTest.cleanupServer()` skips `stopServer()`. The new scheduled executor therefore leaves its non-daemon worker threads alive after the test class finishes. Return `PekkoHttpTestHttp2WebServer` instead of `null` from `setupServer()` so the inherited teardown calls `stop()`.

replies.body: Fixed in 681ea5913e: `setupServer()` now returns `PekkoHttpTestHttp2WebServer`, so the inherited teardown calls `stopServer()` and the completion executor is shut down.

threads.body: [Testing] Both new suites configure the Agrona JVM argument through `targets.all` instead of the required suite-owned `executions.configureEach` API (`.github/instructions/instrumentation-gradle.instructions.md:119–125`). Move this setting into `executions { configureEach { ... } }` and import `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.gradle.executions` so it applies to both default and registered variant executions. Apply the same change to `pekko2Scala3Test` at line 78.
